newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas stable to weak across the board.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas stable to weak across the board.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were steady to soft for most months on Tuesday and lower prices especially in the prompt period and in the third quarter lent the market a bearish tone, traders said.

The gas year from October 1997 was traded at $12.85 pence per therm, compared to deals on Monday at 12.90 and 13.00. But Monday's buyer said that after this deal offers retreated to 13 pence and above, and the market could not be considered substantially weaker.

Prompt prices were also marginally weaker, with day-ahead gas and within-day gas traded at 10.9 pence and 11.15-11.25 pence per therm respectively, compared to deals for Tuesday and Wednesday gas on Monday at around 11.20-11.30 pence.
Dealers said a lower System Average Price had contributed to the prompt weakness.
The third quarter was also slightly weaker, as was the fourth quarter which traded at 13.25-13.325 pence, compared with deals on Monday at 13.40-13.45 pence.
Trade on the IPE was restricted to the first quarter of next year and the volume of business at 75 lots exceeded not only Monday's volume but also last week's entire total of 70 lots.
The market was generally weaker across the board.
